prompt: According to vLLM's contribution guidelines, what triggers the expectation that a contributor open an RFC (design discussion issue) before submitting a PR?
choices: Any PR that touches a file under csrc/
A change exceeding roughly 500 lines of code, excluding kernel, data, config, and test files
Any PR opened by a first-time contributor
A change that modifies more than one Python file

prompt: What mechanism did Hugging Face transformers introduce to cut boilerplate in new model contributions while preserving its 'single model, single file' reading experience for users?
choices: A shared base class every new model must inherit from directly
Modular Transformers: you write a modular_xxx.py file that a linter unravels into the full modeling_xxx.py
A code generator that scaffolds the entire model from a YAML config
Removing the single-file policy entirely in favor of shared attention modules

prompt: You open a 900-line PR to vLLM implementing a new request-scheduling policy, with no prior issue or discussion. What is the most likely outcome?
choices: It merges quickly since scheduling changes are always welcome
CI rejects it immediately for missing a DCO sign-off, unrelated to its size
It gets auto-tagged rfc-required and is unlikely to be reviewed until you open a design discussion issue
A maintainer rewrites it from scratch before merging

prompt: Min-p sampling is a useful case study for this tier because it shows which full arc?
choices: A typo fix that was later expanded into a full model architecture
A community-proposed idea on a GitHub issue that was implemented and merged into two major frameworks (transformers and vLLM) and later formalized in a published paper
A maintainer-only feature that no external contributor was allowed to touch
A change that required a CLA before it could be merged into either project

prompt: Which of the following is the clearest example of a substantive AI-tooling contribution, as opposed to a trivial fix?
choices: Fixing a broken hyperlink in a documentation page
Adding a state-space model architecture like Mamba, requiring new modeling code, bindings to external CUDA kernels, and Trainer-API compatibility
Correcting a misspelled variable name in a comment
Bumping a pinned dependency version in requirements.txt

prompt: In vLLM, what does running `git commit -s` do that matters for getting a PR accepted?
choices: It signs the commit with a GPG key required by GitHub branch protection
It adds the Signed-off-by trailer required to satisfy the project's DCO requirement
It automatically runs the linter before the commit is created
It squashes all prior commits on the branch into one

prompt: In LangChain's package structure, where would a new vector-store integration typically land, versus a change to a core Runnable/LCEL primitive?
choices: Both go through the identical review process since all code lives in one package
The integration goes into langchain-community or a partner package with lighter review; the core primitive change needs broader discussion since it can affect every downstream chain
The integration requires an RFC while core primitive changes do not, since core is rewritten frequently
Neither can be contributed externally; both are maintainer-only

prompt: While your model-contribution PR to transformers is under review, a Hugging Face staff member pushes several commits directly onto your branch to fix formatting and add missing tests, keeping you listed as co-author. What does this most likely indicate?
choices: Your PR is being rejected and taken over without credit
This is a normal, common pattern for promising model PRs — staff finishing the last-mile polish while preserving your authorship
You violated the DCO and the maintainer is correcting it
The PR was auto-flagged as a duplicate and is being merged into someone else's branch
